name: Toshiba JW-10 kana–kanji word processing
description: An office word processor using phonetic phrase entry and conversion to Japanese characters.

impact.note: Its conversion method spread through Japanese society; machine writing of Japanese became practical, and the successors are mainly improved versions of the same idea.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: Toshiba announced the JW-10 Japanese word processor in September 1978.

evidence.supports: IPSJ dates 1978 announcement, February 1979 shipment and reports a price of 6.3 million yen.
The machine supported phrase-based kana–kanji input.

events.caveats: The announcement is distinct from shipping; earlier conversion research and prototypes existed.

contributions.resource: Developed the JW-10 and incorporated phrase-based kana–kanji conversion.

evidence.supports: The machine supported phrase-based kana–kanji input.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: Toshiba began shipping the JW-10 in February 1979.

evidence.supports: IPSJ dates 1978 announcement, February 1979 shipment and reports a price of 6.3 million yen.
The machine supported phrase-based kana–kanji input.

events.caveats: Price is the historical model price, not an observed transaction or a claim of household affordability.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated episode established in cited evidence for this scope, not a global priority claim.
